results.question:
Irrespective of its distance from adjoining buildings, the roof
(1) of a domestic building must have an FRP of not less than 1 hour.
(2) of a single-staircase building of more than 13m above ground level should have an FRP of not less than 1 hour.
(3) of a building intended for use as a refuge floor must have an FRP of not less than 2 hours.
results.responseText:
(1) is **incorrect**. The Code does not impose a blanket rule that every roof of a domestic building must have 1-hour FRR/FRP irrespective of distance from adjoining buildings. Instead, roof FRR is required in specified cases, such as where the roof is close to an adjoining building or site boundary, and then it must be “not less than that of the internal elements of construction,” not automatically 1 hour [Code of Practice for Fire Safety in Buildings (BD), 2011 (2024 Edition), Section 2 - Provisions for Fire Resisting Construction, Clause C5.2(c); Code of Practice for Fire Safety in Buildings (BD), 2011 (2024 Edition), Section 2 - Provisions for Fire Resisting Construction, Clause C5.3(a)-(b)].

(2) is **correct**. For a building with only one required staircase, where the highest floor is more than 13 m above ground level, the roof forming part of the protected exit must have an FRR not less than that of the storey below [Code of Practice for Fire Safety in Buildings (BD), 2011 (2024 Edition), Section 2 - Provisions for Fire Resisting Construction, Clause C12.2]. For domestic use (Use Classification 1 – Residential), the relevant benchmark in Table C1 is 60 minutes, i.e. 1 hour [Code of Practice for Fire Safety in Buildings (BD), 2011 (2024 Edition), Section 2 - Provisions for Fire Resisting Construction, Table C1].

(3) is **correct**. A roof used or intended to be used as a refuge floor must have an FRR not less than that of the storey below [Code of Practice for Fire Safety in Buildings (BD), 2011 (2024 Edition), Section 2 - Provisions for Fire Resisting Construction, Clause C12.3]. The Code’s refuge-floor provisions support a 2-hour standard for refuge floors [Code of Practice for Fire Safety in Buildings (BD), 2011 (2024 Edition), Section 2 - Provisions for Fire Resisting Construction, Clause C17.1].

The answer is C

results.question: Which elements must satisfy stability, integrity, and insulation under FRC Code?
results.responseText:
Under the FRC Code, the key distinction is between **loadbearing elements** and **non-loadbearing fire barriers/enclosures**. The Code states that loadbearing elements are tested to demonstrate the required FRR in terms of **“structural stability, integrity and insulation as appropriate”**; beams and columns are specifically listed as loadbearing elements under the fire test standards, but the Code does **not** say they must always satisfy all three criteria together [Code of Practice for Fire Safety in Buildings (BD), 2011 (2024 Edition), Section 2 – Loadbearing Elements, Clause E3.1]. So **A** is not clearly “must satisfy stability, integrity and insulation” as stated.

For **B** and **C**, the retrieved Table in the FRC provisions shows that a **non-load-bearing compartment wall** and an **enclosure around services in required staircase/protected lobby** require **integrity and insulation**, but **not stability** (“N Y Y”) [Code of Practice for Fire Safety in Buildings (BD), 2011 (2024 Edition), Section 2 - Provisions for Fire Resisting Construction]. Clause C9.3(d) also requires services in required staircases/protected lobbies to be enclosed by fire barriers with FRR not less than the separating walls, reinforcing that these are fire barriers rather than loadbearing elements [Code of Practice for Fire Safety in Buildings (BD), 2011 (2024 Edition), Section 2 - Provisions for Fire Resisting Construction, Clause C9.3(d)].

On the material retrieved, the only option that can correspond to an element requiring all three criteria is **D, structural lift shaft**, because once the shaft is **structural/loadbearing**, it falls within the loadbearing-element regime where **stability, integrity and insulation** are the relevant FRR criteria as appropriate [Code of Practice for Fire Safety in Buildings (BD), 2011 (2024 Edition), Section 2 – Loadbearing Elements, Clause E3.1].

**The answer is D**
